claims.text: Atomic size mismatch governs the high-temperature structural and chemical stability of multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles.
Atomic size mismatch creates local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions act as kinetic barriers to elemental diffusion.
Local lattice distortions inhibit elemental segregation.
The initial materials are multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles produced by physical or chemical fabrication approaches.
Element combinations can be selected to produce nanoparticle groups with high versus low atomic size mismatch.
Large atomic size mismatch increases lattice strain.
Enhanced lattice strain slows atomic diffusion.
Slower atomic diffusion suppresses segregation or phase separation.
Suppression of segregation or phase separation preserves the near-equiatomic solid-solution structure at elevated temperature.
Nanoparticles with higher atomic size mismatch will segregate less than low-mismatch nanoparticles under otherwise identical thermal conditions.
Nanoparticles with higher atomic size mismatch will retain a more uniform elemental distribution over time.
Low-size-mismatch nanoparticles will undergo faster elemental segregation than high-size-mismatch nanoparticles.
Low-size-mismatch nanoparticles will undergo faster phase transformation than high-size-mismatch nanoparticles.
The proposed size-mismatch effect operates over 773–1173 K for catalytic service and 473–1923 K for thermoelectric service.
The size-mismatch effect is most pronounced when nanoparticle surface-energy effects do not dominate bulk entropy contributions.

contradictions.description: The intervention varies atomic size mismatch by choosing different element combinations, whereas the falsification design requires the two groups to have the same overall composition. For fixed elemental identities and fractions, atomic size mismatch cannot ordinarily be varied independently; changing the element combination also changes chemical composition and other properties.

The hypothesis is claimed across 773–1173 K and 473–1923 K, but the stated example experiment tests only 773 K and 473 K. Those tests cannot establish or falsify the claimed behavior across the full temperature boundaries.
